evals.prompt: Read-only protocol extraction from a synthetic methods note (not a real publication): use dataset release R2 with official device-disjoint train/validation/test IDs; a two-layer MLP with width 32; Adam for 100 epochs; report macro AUC averaged over devices. Initialization, normalization and seeds are not specified. I have an external NexuML library and installed core only. Map data/algorithm/training/evaluation into deliverables and checks. Can you fill the gaps with framework defaults and claim exact reproduction? No files, downloads or runs.
evals.expected_output: Maps full protocol to external reusable components/configs and source facts, preserves official device splits/macro scorer, explicitly marks missing choices, does not claim exact reproduction or require base/core checkout.
expectations: Preserves dataset R2, official device-disjoint partitions and macro device AUC rather than replacing them with defaults.
Maps data, algorithm, training and evaluation to user-owned reusable components/recipes and meaningful checks.
Marks initialization, normalization and seeds as unresolved/assumed rather than verified paper facts.

evals.prompt: Read-only fidelity review. In my NexuML recreation, the encoder output matches the reference on 32 inputs. I trained for 3 rather than 100 epochs, used a random split instead of official subject-disjoint splits, and pooled AUC instead of the paper's per-subject macro AUC. My pooled score exceeds the table. Should I mark the paper reproduced and start tuning on its official test results? Give a supported conclusion, corrective checks and baseline/improvement separation. No execution.
evals.expected_output: Limits claim to diagnostic feature parity, identifies training/split/scorer deviations, rejects score-based parity and final-test feedback for selection, preserves separate reproduction/improvement identities.
expectations: Rejects paper-parity/reproduction claims from feature parity on 32 inputs and a higher pooled score.
Identifies all three deviations: training duration, subject-disjoint partitions and macro-versus-pooled scoring.
Rejects official final-test feedback for iterative candidate selection.
Separates a frozen faithful baseline from improvement identities and identifies protocol-level corrective evidence.
